risks: The protocol changes insulin management, with a small risk of hypoglycaemia while fasting; low values are confirmed in the laboratory and treated by the ward's existing policy.
consent: Written informed consent at pre-assessment for the protocol's research data collection and the questionnaire; patients who decline receive usual care and are counted anonymously in the recruitment log.
data: Study charts are coded; the key stays in the pre-assessment clinic; only coded data enter the analysis.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients with limited English receive the dose table in their language and interpreter-supported calls; patients in orthopaedics, who cannot be scheduled first, are reported separately so the protocol is shown to work without scheduling.
effectiveness: Decides whether a multicentre trial is worth running.
efficiency: Uses the nurse's existing hours and the departmental grant.
costs: Study charts, translation of the dose table, and research nurse time within the 12,000 grant.
grants: Departmental grant DRG-2026-09; a multicentre trial would need external funding.
partnerships: Diabetes team, theatre managers for general surgery and urology, two patient partners with insulin-treated diabetes.
rebPath: Hospital research ethics committee review under ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki before any recruitment; the committee has not yet reviewed any version.
limitations: Single site; no comparison group; staff attention may inflate delivery.
summary: Consent at pre-assessment, translated materials, and ethics review before recruitment.
